title: House Floor Debate
subtitle: H.R.4891 — Prescription Drug Price Transparency Act

metadata.laymanSummary: Congress voted to require pharmaceutical companies to publicly disclose how they set drug prices and justify large price increases.

data.billTitle: Prescription Drug Price Transparency Act — Requiring drug makers to justify price increases above inflation

speakers.name: Rep. Kat Cammack
speakers.title: R-FL · House Energy and Commerce
speakers.quote: Americans pay three to ten times more for the same prescription drugs than people in Canada or Germany. Drug companies have no obligation to explain why. This bill fixes that. Transparency is not socialism — it is accountability.

speakers.name: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
speakers.title: D-NY · House Oversight
speakers.quote: Insulin costs $3 to produce. Manufacturers charge $300. That is not a free market — that is an extraction racket. This bill is a first step toward ending the price gouging that is killing Americans who ration their medication.

speakers.name: Rep. Jim Jordan
speakers.title: R-OH · House Judiciary Chair
speakers.quote: Price controls in any form reduce innovation. Pharmaceutical companies invest billions in research and development. If we tell them what they can charge, we are telling them what they can discover. The next cancer cure dies in committee with this kind of legislation.

data.title: What This Vote Means
data.text: H.R.4891 passed 241-190 with notable bipartisan support — 52 Republicans joined all Democrats to pass the bill. It requires pharmaceutical manufacturers to submit annual price justification reports to HHS for any drug whose price increases exceed CPI inflation. Companies refusing to comply face civil penalties. Critics argue it creates a path to de facto price controls.

data.title: Should drug companies be required to justify price increases?

options.label: Yes — prices are out of control
No — it will harm drug development
